key_insight: Compressibility approximations affect simulated atmospheric gravity waves, with fully compressible equations predicting larger high-altitude parcel displacements and greater wavelength and wave-angle differences, especially at low Froude numbers.
engineering_relevance: These differences could alter wind-farm performance predictions in strongly stratified atmospheric conditions.
method: Simulate stratified flow over bell-shaped hills.
Compare linearized Boussinesq, full incompressible Boussinesq, and fully compressible equations.
Evaluate parcel displacement, apparent wavelength, and wave angle.
evidence_signal: The simulations yield qualitatively similar wave structures across formulations but reveal differences attributed to compressibility and nonlinear effects, particularly at low Froude numbers.
watch_item: The abstract reports idealized hill-flow simulations, not direct wind-farm validation or quantified power-prediction errors.
paper_title: Impact of compressiblity approximations on atmospheric gravity wave characteristics
